newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila vows to repel Chinese in shoal.
newsitem.headline: Manila vows to repel Chinese in shoal.

text.p: A Filipino congressional and naval team sailed into Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea on Saturday and vowed to resist any attempts by China to oust them from the disputed rock.
The group, accompanied by the media, unveiled plans to erect a lighthouse on the shoal and develop it into a tourist spot, asserting that the area was part of Philippine territory.
"Whatever happens, we will not leave the place," Navy Captain Ernesto de Leon, who heads a team patrolling the area, told reporters.

Scarborough Shoal, a rock formation running through a 16-km stretch in the South China Sea, sparked a diplomatic row between Beijing and Manila when a group of Filipino fishermen hoisted a Philippine flag and removed Chinese markers on the isle.

The shoal, lying 126 miles (201 km) off Subic freeport in the northern Philippines, is not part of the Spratly islands, a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles and reefs that is also claimed by several countries.
Beijing accused Manila on May 10 of a "serious violation" by raising the Philippine flag in the shoal on April 30.

Four Philippine Navy ships drove away a group of Chinese radio ham operators who disembarked from two Chinese ships to the shoal. "They put a radio (transmitter) in the shoal and made contacts throughout the world," de Leon said.

De leon said the shoal is located in a major shipping route, and used to be a haven for smugglers who used it to unload their wares into small boats. Incidents of smuggling and piracy in the area had dropped with the presence of Navy patrols, he added.
Congressman Roque Ablan, chairman of the House committee on inter-parliamentary relations and diplomacy, said the shoal is 450 miles away from Taiwan and 650 miles from China.
"...It (shoal) can choke to death the commercial traffic between Asia, the United States and the Philippines," he said.

Congressman Jose Yap, chairman of the House committee of Defense, said he will recommend a bill for the development of the area so that "once and for all, we can assert our sovereighty in this shoal."
Besides putting up a light house in the shoal, Ablan said he will propose to Congress to declare the shoal a marine sanctuary because its surrounding area is home to 3,000 species of tropical fish.
De Leon, Ablan, Yap and 15 local and foreign media men took took a 10-hour ride aboard a Navy frigate to the shoal late on Friday.

Later, they transferred to life boats and docked in the shoal for an hour where the officials held a press conference and inspected the Philippine flag raised in a 12-meter metal pipe in one side of the shoal.
